# TinySQL-LM synthetic question-to-SQL dataset

**Purpose:** controlled supervision for a miniature decoder-only transformer trained from scratch. All examples are synthetic, generated by `finetuning.tinysql.data` with seed 42. Generated JSONL files stay outside Git; the generator and compact [data manifest](../experiments/data-manifest.json) are versioned.

## Schemas

`customers(id,name,state)`, `orders(id,customer_id,total,status)`, `products(id,name,category,price)`; the SQL only uses these tables and is intended to run on the deterministic sample database created by `create_db()`.

## Split integrity

| Split | Rows | Source templates |
|---|---:|---|
| train | 6,400 | IDs 0–7 per family (intentional duplicate questions within train) |
| val | 320 | IDs 8–9 per family |
| test | 320 | IDs 10–11 per family |
| challenge | 160 | One different paraphrase pattern per family |

Each row contains `id`, `family`, `template_id`, `question`, `sql`, and `values`.

Train/validation/test/challenge sets have no identical natural-language question *across splits*. SQL output programs and family structures **do recur** across splits. Therefore, this is **paraphrase-held-out**, not a novel-program or novel-schema benchmark. Your experiments should report this caveat prominently.

Original training contains **6,400 rows but 1,968 unique questions**. Adapter augmentation
contains **15,930 rows but 3,525 unique questions**. Repetition is preserved for historical
reproducibility; row counts are not counts of independent observations.

## Training signals

The task-specific tokenizer is learned from train text only. Question/schema tokens are context; loss is applied exclusively to output SQL tokens. The model is evaluated using raw autoregressive decoding on two independently seeded, populated SQLite databases.

## Data ethics

No customer-identifying information or personal data is used; all customers, orders and products are fabricated. The vocabulary of states/categories/statuses and fixed grammar is intentionally tiny. Results should **not** be extrapolated to real-world business SQL without external validation.

## Regeneration

```bash
uv run --project .. --no-sync python -m finetuning.tinysql.data --out runs/regenerated-data --train 6400 --val 320 --test 320 --challenge 160
```
